description: CONVERG. AND SPECIAL SUPPORT PROGRAM-SUSTAINABLE INFRA. PROJS. ALLEVIATING GAPS (SIPAG)-SIPAG-ACCESS ROADS AND/OR BRIDGES FROM THE NATL. ROADS LEADING TO MAJOR/ STRAT. PUBLIC BLDGS./FACILITIES-CONST. OF ROAD, PHASE IV, SITIO TALAMSI I-SITIO KAMBUBUYUGAN,
colour_meaning: Check: not scored. Either a tested “looks fine on paper” pattern, or a single weak sign (for example an unusual price) that alone is not enough to score.

items.label: Very fast award after bid opening
items.detail: Award made 8 days after the bid deadline (past road contracts awarded this fast had about twice the odds of termination)

items.label: Two bidders
items.detail: 2 bidder(s) recorded. Not linked to failed contracts in past data, so not scored.

items.label: Total budget above the 95th percentile (length not stated)
items.detail: Official budget ₱144.7M with no stated length; the 95th percentile for Access / tourism road is ₱99.0M.

items.label: Road contracts from other agencies (PhilGEPS)
items.detail: Jmld Construction also won 5 road contract(s) worth ₱14.3M from 3 other procuring entities (2022–2024), e.g. Barangay Mambulo Viejo, Libmanan, Camarines Sur, City Of Naga, Camarines Sur, Metropolitan Naga Water District. PhilGEPS awards record no outcome, so this is not scored.

items.detail: 44% of Bulacan's elected local positions were held by fat-dynastic officials after the 2025 election (44% in 1992); median province 28%; largest clan: Cruz (4.2% of positions); family poverty incidence 5% (2012).

items.detail: 79% of elected officials in the province have potential dynastic links (national average 54.5%; broader name matching than the Ateneo measure).

items.detail: Agay Cruz, Danny Domingo, Arthur Robes, Linabelle Villarica, Cholo Violago (Ateneo dataset).

assessment.derivation: 0 strong + 1 weak signal → below Medium (needs 1 strong or 2 weak); a single weak sign is shown as a Blue check case.

steps.title: Confirm the basic facts on the official DPWH page
sub: Budget, location, status, dates and bidders match this page.

steps.title: Open the bid documents
sub: Look for the quantities, a Bill of Quantities and technical specifications.

steps.title: Read Claude's check and confirm its points against the sources
Verify the risk: Procurement competition and bidding patterns
sub: Compare the bid-opening date with the Notice of Award date.
Ask whether post-qualification (checking the winner's documents and capacity) could be done that fast.

steps.title: Check site and field evidence
sub: Check the site before work starts: satellite imagery of the stretch, earlier contracts on the same road, and whether a local monitor (Bisto Proyekto, a TPM civil-society partner) can take geotagged photos later.

steps.title: Write down what you found and keep the documents you relied on
sub: Screenshots, Bill of Quantities pages, photos or letters: attach them with your decision.

docs_note:
**Documents (advice only):** The readable text gives the project title and the standard bidding template, but no quantities, lengths or specifications; the Bill of Quantities is listed in the contents but its figures were not extracted, so scope cannot be confirmed.
**Unusual compared with the standard Philippine Bidding Documents:** none found; several template brackets (for example bid security amounts and licences) are still unfilled, which is common in DPWH documents.
